    Changelog

    emss 0.1.0.9000

    • The package is renamed from EmStanS to emss. Use library(emss) and emss::; function names, including emstans(), are unchanged.

    Stage 3: method decisions and argument names

    Changes to results

    • An item’s empirical (operational) level is now 1 + the number of cut scores at or below its location, the rule the estimation itself uses. Previously it was assigned by the item’s position relative to the cut items, and two cuts on the same item were merged into one, so the items at and above them were placed one level too low. Cut scores are unchanged; agreement, crosstabs and item review change only when two cuts fall on the same item: in the example studies, 58 items in 19 grade results (mostly CAAELP and ESS-Count).
    • bootstrapping() now resamples items and takes the exact ESS minimum in every sample, the same estimator as emstans(). The earlier bootstrap (a jittered grid of candidate cuts with a GAM-smoothed minimum) remains available with grid = "jittered"; it now uses one grid per sample for all cut levels (each level previously drew its own grid but was reported on level 2’s grid points).
    • The item-review distance is unchanged (“location - (upper cut - 1)”).

    New argument names

    • emstans(file, data, ..., grades, location, method, smooth, by_domain, domains, font_size, digits). Former names still work, with one warning listing the replacements: filePath -> file, grade -> grades, loc -> location, WESS = TRUE/FALSE -> method = "weight"/"count", gamest -> smooth, domain/select_domain -> by_domain/domains, targets -> ess_data(columns = ...), and median (not needed). Arguments after data must be named in full, so a former name is never partially matched to a new one (domain would otherwise have been taken as domains). Misspelled arguments are an error.
    • by_domain = TRUE always includes the all-items unit of each grade.
    • bootstrapping(x, unit, n = 100, seed = NULL, grid = c("items", "jittered")); gca_name and boot_num still work, with a warning.
    • Dependencies dropped: glue, purrr.

    Stage 2: new structure

    New input options

    • ess_data() builds the input from data frames or CSV files with any column names: columns are mapped by name or position with columns =. Only ratings and items are required; level labels, SD and EC can come from a setup table, from the levels, sd and ec arguments, or both (arguments win). ess_read_excel() reads the emss workbook by sheet name. emstans(data = ) accepts either, or the old list of data frames.
    • Level labels are carried through to every table, plot and report, in level order, and may differ by grade.
    • Ratings with several rounds are analysed separately by grade and round (units such as R1-All Round 2).
    • plot() draws the inconsistency profile of a unit’s modal result, or cut scores and impact across grades.

    Changes to results

    • When a cut level had tied minima, the old cal_minp() mixed its candidates with other levels’ (a matrix(byrow = TRUE) on column-ordered data). A level could then get another level’s cut, which need not be a minimum for it at all: in one study, a level-3 cut was placed where 48 items were inconsistent instead of at the unique minimum with 21. The tie rule (lower weight, then lower count, then earlier item) is now applied to each level separately. Ties are common under ESS-Count, whose counts are integers: across the example studies 57 of 840 grade-level cuts changed, 48 under Count and 9 under Weight. The bug predates Stage 1. Running the old code with only this fix gives exactly the new cut scores.
    • The EC-adjusted crosstab took level numbers from the levels present in a grade (the same bug fixed in the item review in Stage 1).
    • Averages are rounded once from exact values; the old code rounded to 4 decimals first, which moved one average cut in the Maine study by 0.01.

    Changes to the result object

    • emstans() returns plain tables (panelist, modal, median and average cuts; agreement; item review; impact) plus the input data and settings. Code that read internal elements such as res$tab1 must use extract().
    • extract() returns long tables with level labels; extract(res, "cutscore") names each cut by the level it opens (for example M, L).
    • bootstrapping() gains a seed argument and reports the underlying error when every sample fails. Its results are tables from extract(); the Excel export (boot_excel()) was removed.

    Performance and size

    • No HTML is built when emstans() runs; report() builds it on demand. Every example study now runs in about a second or less, including the report (previously up to 47 seconds).
    • About 4,400 lines of code removed. Dependencies dropped: foreach, ggrepel, grid, kableExtra, tidyr, tidyselect, magrittr; knitr moved to Suggests.

    Stage 1

    Changes to results

    • Cut scores are now taken from the exact minimum of the ESS inconsistency profile. Previously the profile (weights divided by SD) was rounded to two decimals before the minimum was found, which created false ties and could pick a different cut. Across the example studies this changed 30 of 634 grade-level cuts, mostly on theta-scale locations with a scale-score SD, where the rounding merged real differences. Values are still rounded to nine decimals before comparison, which removes floating-point noise only, so ties in the exact profile are still broken by the lower count, then the lower cut.

    Bug fixes

    • The package installs on case-sensitive file systems (macOS, Linux): the stale Collate field in DESCRIPTION has been removed.
    • Examinee data in the wide layout (repeated Score/Freq/Grade blocks) is read again.
    • The item review no longer drops a grade that has no inconsistent items, which made emstans() fail for such grades.
    • The item review takes level numbers from the level labels, so grades in which no item is aligned to some level are compared at the right level.
    • Levels numbered 10 and above are parsed correctly.
    • update() matches manual cut scores to grades by name, so argument order no longer matters; unknown grade names and wrong numbers of cuts are errors. Its first argument is now object, matching the generic.
    • Item locations are attached to ratings by Item_ID rather than by row position.

    Input checks

    • emstans() now stops with a clear message when the location column is missing, non-numeric or incomplete, when item IDs are duplicated, when SD or EC are not numbers, when an ALD label is not one of the grade’s Level Options (previously it became LevelNA), or when a panelist did not rate every item in the grade exactly once.

    Performance

    • ESS-Count and ESS-Weight profiles are computed with sorted cumulative sums instead of an items x candidates table (identical results; 30x to 3,700x faster for that step, depending on test length).
    • Modal ALDs across panelists are computed for all items at once (identical results; about 1,000x faster for that step).
    • End to end, typical studies run about 2x faster.

    Tests

    • Added a testthat suite: hand-computed and brute-force checks of the Count/Weight profiles and the selection rule, equivalence of the modal ALD rule, input validation, update() by name, and a snapshot of cut scores on simulated data.
